methods.name: Peer-Median

data.narrative:
LeydenJar Technologies is a Series B climate and energy company that has raised €23M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (KoBold Metals at $3.0B Series C, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B Series C, and Amogy at $700M Series C), supplemented by reference to 9 total private comparables and 1 public peer (LNZA).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the €23M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage transitions, implying a valuation of $44M. Peer-median analysis calculates the median valuation across the 3-company sample, yielding $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. The divergence reflects stage compression—the comparable set comprises Series C companies trading at material premiums to LeydenJar's current Series B position.

Triangulation across both methods produces a range of $37M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median estimate of $522M. The wide spread reflects fundamental uncertainty about LeydenJar's technology readiness relative to later-stage peers and prospective capital intensity. The peer-median approach suggests significant upside potential conditional on achieving Series C milestones; the stage-progression method provides a more conservative floor tied to demonstrated investor commitment.
